purpose: Share strict readiness-marker parsing between lifecycle host fixtures and their parent tests.
behavior: parseMarker considers only newline-terminated lines and returns undefined until the named marker is complete.
Requires exactly the requested count of distinct positive integer PID tokens separated by single internal spaces; malformed markers return Error.
untilTree consumes fixture lines until READY and every numbered descendant level have appeared, returns PIDs in level order and leaves the loop.
contracts: Premature output end is an error; no sleep substitutes for readiness.
Helpers are side-effect free so importing them does not install host hooks.
failures_or_limits: Number conversion does not explicitly check Number.isSafeInteger for PID text.

purpose: Run registered binding assertions sequentially with failure-counting deadlines.
behavior: test appends name/function pairs; runTests races each function with a default 20-second timeout.
Logs ok or FAIL per case, clears its timer and continues after failure.
Calls finish with passed/failed counts, OS/runtime and status one if any test failed.
contracts: Timeout is always a failure; test functions are not canceled when the timeout wins.
failures_or_limits: The harness's summary is computed during execution; none was produced here.

purpose: Assert static inference and prohibited operations in the public TypeScript declarations.
behavior: Checks pipe/terminal overload selection and rejects resize on pipes, closeStdin on PTYs, stdin on run and input on spawn.
Checks default/true text output as string, false as Uint8Array and dynamic boolean as a union, including both child kinds.
Asserts the closed OmniError code union and exhaustive Exit reason union including memory_exceeded.
Exercises AsyncDisposable, await using and typed async chunk/line iteration; @ts-expect-error makes unexpectedly accepted misuse fail compilation.
contracts: The file explicitly states nothing here runs; tsc -p test/tsconfig.json is its intended validation.
failures_or_limits: Static type acceptance cannot establish startup/cleanup/runtime behavior; compilation was not run.

purpose: Classify conformance failures and compare every declared expectation without loose coercion.
behavior: Fail distinguishes product from harness; unclassified exceptions become harness failures and non-OmniError library throws become product failures.
check requires expected fields to exist, matches error codes/messages/partial results, and includes elapsedMs.
Strict scalar matchers support numeric bounds, text/bytes contains/regex/length/hex, nested fields and exact line-piece sequences.
Process entries match an unordered one-to-one assignment with exact cardinality, supporting PID captures and null parents.
contracts: Only product failures may later become pending; malformed expectations remain harness failures.
Text length counts Unicode code points, binary length counts bytes; string equality compares UTF-8 bytes.

purpose: Represent the explicit pending conformance ledger and reject stale or malformed exemptions.
behavior: Parses nonblank, non-comment lines as exactly an item ID and work-package ID, recording malformed and duplicate lines.
item maps a scenario suffix to its parent C-* item; pending is simple membership.
After a suite, check rejects ledger IDs with no scenario and entries whose applicable scenarios all passed.
contracts: Full-line comments start with #; extra tokens are invalid rather than inline comments.
Known but nonapplicable items are not treated as passing.
failures_or_limits: The ledger authorizes only product-failure deferral; harness classification is enforced elsewhere.

purpose: Provide independent OS liveness evidence and canonical temporary directories to the runner.
behavior: Linux reads /proc/PID/stat, treating ENOENT/ESRCH and Z/X as dead; unrecognized states or read errors are unknown.
macOS/Unix uses ps with strict output/status conditions; Windows uses tasklist CSV, accepting an INFO no-match line as dead.
expectLife polls every 20 ms until all PIDs match or the bound expires, immediately raising harness failure for an unknown observation.
tmp creates a scenario-specific directory, resolves macOS path aliases and removes Windows extended-path prefixes.
contracts: Liveness mismatch is product failure; observation inability is harness failure and cannot count as dead.
No product API is used as the liveness oracle.
failures_or_limits: Tasklist's no-match recognition depends on INFO: text; unavailable or unexpected output fails closed.

purpose: Restrict scenario regular expressions to the intended common JS/Rust subset.
behavior: Scans syntax before compiling with the JavaScript u flag; supports ordinary groups, noncapturing groups, basic quantifiers, selected classes and numeric escapes.
Rejects lookarounds, named groups, flags, backreferences, unsupported escapes, nested/set-operation classes, surrogate escapes and malformed quantifier positions.
checkTable requires accepted and refused cases, verifies positive/negative matches and capture group 1, and reports every mismatch.
contracts: The differential regex table is mandatory before the contract runner starts scenarios.
Invalid patterns throw diagnostic errors naming the pattern/construct.
dependencies: Rust runner's regex engine is the parity boundary.
failures_or_limits: The scanner and differential table cover a deliberate subset, not all JS or Rust regex syntax.

evidence.quote:
/**
 * The subset: literals; `^ $ | * + ? *? +? ??`; `{n}` `{n,}` `{n,m}`; `( )` and `(?: )`; classes without nesting, set
 * operators or ranges next to a class escape; escapes `\d \D \w \W` (`\d \w` inside a class), `\n \r \t \f \v`, `\xHH`,
 * `\uHHHH` (not a surrogate), and escaped syntax characters (`\-` only inside a class, as under the `u` flag).
 * Everything else (look-around, backreferences, named groups, flags, `\s`, `\b`, `\p`, Rust-only syntax) is refused.

purpose: Read scenario output with stable consumers, complete-line matching and loss accounting.
behavior: Keeps an iterator and per-stream partial lines across read steps; a new mode tries a new claim and only replaces the old iterator after successful next().
Captures regex group 1 or full match and checks until against completed lines; chunks split LF and strip one CR, while line mode joins continues pieces.
Gaps and stream end finish partial lines; all items in a consumed chunk belong to the current step even after its until match.
Copies byte buffers, accumulates stream data/chunk/loss/continuation/piece counters, optionally returns the iterator on detach and reports child.droppedBytes.
contracts: Ending before the required match count is product failure; unknown stream or data type is product failure.
Read-step output is local to that step although partial line/capture state persists.
failures_or_limits: Lossy UTF-8 decoding is used for regex/capture text; raw returned bytes remain available in byte mode.

purpose: Fully validate scenario structure and dataflow before invoking the product.
behavior: Requires filename/id agreement, a recognized C-item scenario ID, allowed OS/language selectors, text files and nonempty steps.
Each step must contain exactly one of ten actions plus only its permitted keys.
Tracks pipe/PTY/asynchronous-run handles and built-in/captured variables; rejects undefined use, closing a PTY, resizing a non-PTY or missing read-until/OS-PIDs.
Checks every step before execution, including later steps that could otherwise be hidden by an early pending failure.
contracts: run as goes exactly with await:false; resize dimensions must fit 16 bits.
Expectation substitutions may reference variables defined by the same step after define is applied.
failures_or_limits: Name definition overwrites maps rather than explicitly rejecting duplicate handle names; scenario file paths are not confinement-validated here.

purpose: Validate action values, options and matchers as harness input before scenario execution.
behavior: Checks command arrays, count/boolean/text fields, capture regexes, positive until-match counts and hex payloads.
Restricts expectations by action, requires error when using message/result, and validates nested process entries, loss fields and line pieces.
Allows exceptional numeric option stimuli through {$number:NaN/Infinity/-Infinity}; rejects unknown keys/options.
The enumerated reason list stops at aborted, and option list lacks maxRssBytes/backpressure despite their presence in the current public binding.
contracts: Malformed input is a harness failure and must never become pending.
This schema intentionally validates test DSL types separately from product invalid-value tests.
dependencies: native/omni/bindings/node/index.d.ts provides the broader current API.
failures_or_limits: A shared JSON scenario cannot express memory_exceeded, maxRssBytes or backpressure through this schema as written; separate tests may cover them.

purpose: Execute validated scenario steps with explicit state, bounds and cleanup.
behavior: Creates temporary files and built-in variables, then executes ten public-API/OS actions with a shared AbortController.
Each step defaults to ten seconds; OS timeout is harness failure and library-operation timeout is product failure.
Stores spawned handles or loose children, asynchronous run outcomes, consumers and captured values; resolves whole captures to lists and embedded captures to their first value.
Finally aborts and zero-grace-stops every child in parallel with a five-second best-effort bound, then removes the temporary directory.
contracts: Only OmniError becomes an expected error outcome; unexpected library exceptions become product failures.
write without data defaults to stdin close and cannot close a terminal; wait on an asynchronous run consumes its stored handle.
dependencies: runner/scenario.mjs, read.mjs, expect.mjs, os.mjs and schema.mjs.
failures_or_limits: Cleanup ignores stop failures and timeout; it prevents harness hangs but is not itself an asserted tree-death proof.

purpose: Select and judge every TypeScript scenario against the pending ledger.
behavior: Sorts JSON files, fails an empty directory, parses each complete scenario before OS/language filtering and counts other selectors separately.
Runs applicable scenarios sequentially and aggregates whether every run of each item passed.
Only product failures with ledger membership count as pending; schema, runner and oracle failures append errors.
Rejects a suite where no scenario ran and adds unknown/stale ledger findings before returning all counts.
contracts: Malformed scenarios cannot hide behind selection or a pending item.
Only returned errors determine failure at the entry point.
failures_or_limits: No suite invocation occurred; counts are algorithmic definitions rather than observed results.

purpose: Centralize binding test runtime selection, binary discovery and explicit process completion.
behavior: Detects Bun before Deno, otherwise Node, and resolves the Omni repository root from this module.
Resolves fixture/supervisor from explicit environment or target/debug with Windows suffix; missing binaries throw and supervisor is written back to JS process.env.
Loads index.js through createRequire; hostCommand adds Deno -A and runtime-specific exposed-GC flags.
finish flushes a summary line then process.exit(code), so finished suites cannot be retained by a live child.
contracts: CARGO_TARGET_DIR changes checkout lookup; absent binaries are failures, never skips.
failures_or_limits: Explicit suite termination is test harness policy rather than production process-lifetime behavior.

purpose: Probe the contract runner itself with positive controls, mutants and malformed scenarios.
behavior: A scripted fake API/child drives every step and matcher, including binary input, captures, process entries, detach, gap/continuation and abort.
Mutants assert wrong values/types, unexpected errors, missing markers, duplicate process matching and nonending waits fail as product errors with step context.
Malformed JSON, regex, variables, files, handles and action combinations remain harness failures even for a pending item; ledger tests reject stale/unknown/duplicate entries.
Also asserts regex-table negative controls, real self/dead PID observation, OS parser unknown states, strict host marker parsing and readiness detachment.
contracts: Fake library tests establish runner sensitivity, not the native library's behavior.
Historical W00-red rationale does not describe the current implementation state.
dependencies: OS process probes for the oracle controls.
failures_or_limits: No positive control or mutant was executed here.

evidence.quote:
test("positive control: a correct library passes a scenario that uses every kind of step and matcher", async () => {
  const gone = spawnSync(process.execPath, ["--version"]).pid; // reaped: the OS says dead
  const steps = [
    { run: ["x", "a"], options: { env: { K: "v" }, timeoutMs: 5 }, expect: { ...EXIT, stdout: { hex: "68690a" }, stderr: { length: 0 }, elapsedMs: { gte: 0, lt: 5000 } } },
    { run: ["x"], expect: { stdout: { contains: "i\n" }, stderr: { regex: "^$" }, exitCode: { gte: 0, lt: 1 } } },
    { run: ["x"], options: { timeoutMs: { $number: "NaN" } }, expect: { error: "INVALID_ARGUMENT", message: ["timeout"] } },
    { run: ["x"], options: { text: false, input: { hex: "00ff" } }, expect: { stdout: { hex: "00ff" } } },
    { spawn: ["x"], as: "c" },
    { read: "c", until: { match: "^READY$" }, capture: { p: "^PID (\\d+)$" }, expect: { stdout: "PID 4242\nREADY\nmore\n", chunks: 3, droppedBytes: { stdout: 3 } } },
    { processes: "c", capture: "all", expect: { entries: [{ pid: 4243, parentPid: "${p}", name: { regex: "^fake\\d$" } }, { pid: "${p}", parentPid: null, name: "fake" }] } },
    { os: "alive", pids: ["${c.pid}"] },
    { os: "dead", pids: [gone] },
    { read: "c", until: "end", detach: true, expect: { stdout: "tail", chunks: 1 } },
    { read: "c", until: "end", expect: { error: "INVALID_ARGUMENT" } },
    { stop: "c", graceMs: 10, expect: { reason: "killed", success: false } },
    { spawn: ["x"], as: "d" },
    { read: "d", lines: true, until: "end", expect: { stdout: "a\nbbc\n\n", chunks: 4, continues: 1, lostBefore: 5, pieces: { stdout: [{ bytes: 1, continues: false }, { bytes: 2, continues: true }, { bytes: 1, continues: false }, { bytes: 0, continues: false }] } } },
    { abort: "d" },
    { run: ["x"], expect: { error: "ABORTED" } },
  ];
  assert.equal(await failure(fakeApi(), steps), null);

purpose: Isolate worker termination so host crashes and tree leaks become parent-test observations.
behavior: Main environment loads the API and completes a fixture run, then starts worker.mjs in live or idle mode.
Waits for the worker's message/error, verifies its run output and awaits worker.terminate().
Queries each reported PID through the OS while the host still lives, then prints termination PIDs and states.
contracts: Liveness must be checked before the host itself exits, because host death would independently clean trees.
Expected normal host exit and dead states are asserted by hardening.mjs.
failures_or_limits: The historical Bun rc134 comment is background, not current runtime evidence.

purpose: Load the addon in a worker environment and report a controlled live tree or idle state.
behavior: Completes a fixture run emitting from-worker.
In live mode spawns tree=1/ready/hang, waits for the descendant marker and posts root/descendant PIDs; idle mode posts an empty PID list.
contracts: Parent controls termination; the worker reports readiness but does not assert cleanup.
failures_or_limits: No worker environment was started in this analysis.
